findings.fix: Set lang to a valid code for the page's actual language, for example lang="en".
findings.violation: The lang attribute value "translanguage" is not a valid BCP 47 language code, so browsers and assistive technology cannot determine what language the page is in.

findings.fix: Add descriptive title text, for example "Rider service updates".
findings.location: the title element in the head
findings.violation: The page title is empty, so browser tabs, bookmarks, browser history, and screen reader page announcements all show no name for this page.

findings.fix: Add an alt attribute describing the image's content, or alt="" if it is purely decorative.
findings.location: the image at the end of the "Fare adjustments" section
findings.violation: The image has no alt attribute at all, so anyone who cannot see it gets no information about what it shows.

findings.evidence: "Riders can check real time arrivals at any station kiosk. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Rewrite or remove the second sentence so it actually follows from checking real time arrivals at a kiosk.
findings.location: second paragraph of the "Fare adjustments" section
findings.violation: The second sentence refers to "the same request," but the paragraph never describes a request, only a self-service action of checking arrivals, so the sentence reads as leftover text from a different paragraph.

findings.fix: Change this heading to h2, matching the level of the other top-level section headings.
findings.violation: The heading level jumps from h1 and h2 straight to h4, skipping h3, which breaks the logical heading outline of the page.

findings.evidence: "Passengers can report a service issue by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Replace the second sentence with text describing what happens after a service issue is reported, or remove it.
findings.location: first paragraph of the "Accessibility improvements" section
findings.violation: The second sentence describes schedule page updates, which does not follow from reporting a service issue by phone, suggesting a sentence copied from a different paragraph.

findings.fix: Add a caption element identifying the table, for example "Zone status".
findings.location: the zone status table in the "Accessibility improvements" section
findings.violation: The table has no caption, so its purpose is not announced to anyone who cannot infer it from the surrounding page context.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the online portal. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Remove the second sentence or replace it with wording relevant to checking arrivals online.
findings.location: the status card in the "Station updates" section
findings.violation: The second sentence describes a confirmation for a processed request, but checking real time arrivals is not a request that gets processed, making the sentence a non sequitur.

findings.evidence: "Choose a plan" / "Enter payment details" / "Confirm your order"
findings.fix: Remove this block if it belongs to a different page, or add a heading and explanatory text tying it to the surrounding content.
findings.location: the wizard-steps block in the "Station updates" section
findings.violation: This three step checkout and payment sequence has no stated connection to the surrounding content about station and fare updates, and it appears with no heading or explanation of what plan or order it refers to.

findings.fix: Change the link text to something descriptive, such as "view the full list of upcoming adjustments".
findings.location: the link at the end of the "Station updates" section
findings.violation: The link text "click here" does not describe where the link goes, so it is meaningless when read out of context, for example in a list of links or by a screen reader.

findings.fix: Add the required attribute to the phone input so its behavior matches the label text.
findings.location: the phone number field in the station updates form
findings.violation: The label text states the field is required, but the input itself has no required attribute, so the form's actual validation does not enforce what the label claims.

findings.evidence: Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.
findings.fix: Only set aria-invalid to true after a failed validation attempt, and add aria-describedby pointing at the error span's id so the error is tied to the input for assistive technology too.
findings.location: the promo code field in the station updates form
findings.violation: The promo field is marked aria-invalid="true" and shows an error message before the user has entered anything, and the error text is not linked to the input by aria-describedby, so the two are only related visually, not programmatically.

findings.evidence: <button type="submit" class="btn-primary" id="s3-form-submit" aria-label="Send form now">Submit</button>
findings.fix: Remove the aria-label so the accessible name matches the visible text, or change the visible text to match the aria-label.
findings.location: the submit button in the station updates form
findings.violation: The button's visible text reads "Submit" but its accessible name is overridden to "Send form now" by aria-label, so sighted users and screen reader users are given different names for the same control.
